newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares head lower after three-day rally.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares head lower after three-day rally.

text.p: Egyptian share prices retreated on Sunday after investors took advantage of the higher prices of the last three days to sell their holdings.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its all-share index fell for the first time since Tuesday by 2.83 points to 359.81 points. The index was 362.64 points on Thursday, its highest level in almost 10 days.

Turnover was an average 53.82 million pounds ($15.85 million). Thirty-nine 39 shares of the total 86 shares traded during the day ended lower while 23 other stocks rose, with the remaining 24 stocks closing unchanged.
"The higher prices of the last three days have encouraged people to sell, this fall is expected," said broker Ehab el-Mahallawi at securities firm Intercapital.
"It's also Sunday so the foreign institutions are out of the market. They do make a difference," he added.

Brokers said many investors were also liquidating their holdings to get into new public share offerings by the government which has adopted privatisation as the flagship of its economic reform programme.

The state on Sunday offered from 10 to 75 percent of its holding in Simo/Middle East Paper company at a minimum price of 20 pounds a share and it also said it would soon offer investors at least 10 percent of its stake in Alexandria Flour Mills at a minimum price of 75 pounds a share.
Approaching dividend distributions also affected trading in the market, brokers said.

Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries was the most active share, climbing five pounds to 208 after shares worth 10.5 million pounds changed hands. Brokers said many investors were trying to buy the share because of the attached 13 pound dividend for 1996.

Suez Cement ended one pound lower at 66 pounds after busy trading and brokers attributed the slight slippage to investor disappointment with the firm's 4.50 pound for 1996. Suez Cement gave out 5.20 pounds for each of its 49 million shares in the previous year.

Other cement firms also featured prominently in Sunday's trading. Helwan Portland Cement was the day's second most active share, with 7.83 million pounds of turnover but the stock closed 1.45 pounds lower at 73.05.

Brokers said institutional interest in North Cairo Flour Mills helped push share prices five pounds higher to 180 pounds. Their interest spilled over onto Upper Egypt Flour Mills which also rose 1.55 to 82 pounds.
Commercial International Bank (CIB), which was heavily traded last week after a disappointing dividend announcement, ended 0.5 pounds lower at 72.2.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 505.54 points from 510.89 points on Thursday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also slipped to 262.66 from 264.35 points.
